title: Choosing the appropriate Rule 12 response
summary: Rule 12 provides distinct ways to respond to a complaint, including objections to authority, legal sufficiency, excessive vagueness, and specified material within the pleading. Each motion has its own purpose and preservation rules.
notes: A Rule 12(b)(6) motion and a Rule 56 motion use different materials and assumptions. The full text of Rule 12 is in the supplement on file (PDF page 33), linked below.

sections.Meaning: Rule 12 provides distinct ways to respond to a complaint, including objections to authority, legal sufficiency, excessive vagueness, and specified material within the pleading. Each motion has its own purpose and preservation rules.
sections.How to work through the question: Identify whether the objection concerns jurisdiction, service, venue, failure to state a claim, a required party, inability to frame a response, or matter to be struck. Garcia illustrates why a court may preserve a claim while requiring detail and removing particular allegations.
